prompt: Three identical machines working together produce $120$ parts in $4$ hours. At the same rate, how many parts will five of these machines produce in $6$ hours?
hint: Find the output of one machine in one hour first.

hints.text: Find the output of one machine in one hour first.
$120$ parts came from $3 \times 4 = 12$ machine-hours, so the rate is $10$ parts per machine-hour.
$5$ machines for $6$ hours is $30$ machine-hours: $30 \times 10 = 300$ parts.

learningObjective: Solve a work-rate problem by reducing to a single-unit rate.
explanation: Total effort is machines × hours: $3 \times 4 = 12$ machine-hours produced $120$ parts.
The new scenario is $5 \times 6 = 30$ machine-hours, giving $30 \times 10 = 300$ parts.

alternativeExplanations.title: Scale the two factors separately
steps: Going from $3$ machines to $5$ multiplies output by $\tfrac{5}{3}$.
Going from $4$ hours to $6$ multiplies it by $\tfrac{6}{4} = \tfrac{3}{2}$.
$120 \times \tfrac{5}{3} \times \tfrac{3}{2} = 300$. Both routes work; the machine-hour route is harder to get backwards.
